key_insight: Medical Heuristic Learning (MHL) replaces opaque model training with an LLM-guided process that turns clinical tabular prediction into explicit, executable, and auditable decision rules.
clinical_relevance: This could make clinical decision support systems easier to inspect, update, and trust, especially in small, imbalanced, or evolving medical datasets.
method: LLM-driven workflow combines statistical probes, medical knowledge probes, rule synthesis, and iterative code refinement.
Outputs versioned pure-Python decision rules rather than learned weights.
Supports continual learning by revising previously validated rules when features or documentation change.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports comprehensive experiments on medical datasets showing performance comparable to state-of-the-art methods, with strong behavior in small-sample and highly imbalanced settings and reduced catastrophic forgetting under feature evolution.
watch_item: Because the system depends on rule synthesis and iterative updates, real-world deployment may require careful validation to avoid brittle rules or inconsistencies across changing clinical workflows.
paper_title: Medical Heuristic Learning: An LLM-Driven Framework for Interpretable and Auditable Clinical Decision Rules
